title: Erdős's edge-count sufficient condition for Hamiltonicity
statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, and let $\delta$ denote its minimum degree. If $6\delta \le n$ and
\[
\binom{n-\delta}{2} + \delta^2 < m,
\]
then $G$ is Hamiltonian, that is, $G$ contains a cycle passing through every vertex exactly once. (P. Erdős)
hypotheses_covered: minimum degree bounded by a sixth of the vertex count: $6\delta \le n$
replaced:

\textbf{4.2.8} Show that if $G$ is simple with $\nu \ge 6\delta$ and $\varepsilon >
\binom{\nu-\delta}{2} + \delta^2$, then $G$ is hamiltonian. (P. Erd\"os)
